name: Juan María Herrera Martín
group: Radiofrequency, Electromagnetics, Microwaves and Antennas Group
researchLine: Integrated RF front ends and antennas for space, sensing, and future communications.
heroSummary: I design silicon-germanium front ends and antennas at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths, combining electromagnetic simulation, fabrication-aware integration, and laboratory characterization. My work supports radiometry and Earth observation, nanosatellite communications, automotive sensing, SATCOM, and emerging 6G systems.
shortBio: I am a PhD candidate in Signal Processing and Communications Engineering at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid and a researcher in GREMA. My work focuses on integrated silicon-germanium front ends, antennas, radiometry, and high-frequency measurement for space, Earth observation, automotive sensing, SATCOM, and 6G. I completed a doctoral research stay at Aalto University and teach RF and network-analysis laboratory courses at UC3M. I also contribute to student-led space and telecommunications initiatives through PUNTO, UC3-Base, BOIRA, and STAR UC3M.
longBio: I am a PhD candidate in Signal Processing and Communications Engineering at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid (UC3M), where I have worked as research personnel in the Radiofrequency, Electromagnetics, Microwaves and Antennas Group (GREMA) since 2021. My doctoral research develops on-chip silicon-germanium front ends at frequencies above 200 GHz and laboratory methods for electromagnetic and electrical characterization.

My broader research connects integrated antennas, radiometry, circular polarization, phased arrays, and high-frequency measurement with applications in Earth observation, nanosatellite telemetry and telecommand, automotive sensing, satellite communications, and emerging 6G systems. In 2024, I completed a funded doctoral research stay at Aalto University focused on millimeter-wave, terahertz, and optical systems for biomedical and space applications.

I hold a double master's degree in Telecommunications Engineering and Space Engineering and a bachelor's degree in Sound and Image Engineering from UC3M. My academic record includes an FPU doctoral fellowship, the UC3M Extraordinary End of Degree Award, and SENER Foundation awards for my radiometer-antenna thesis and the BOIRA satellite predesign. I teach laboratory courses in high-frequency technology, radiofrequency subsystems, and linear network analysis, and have co-tutored a bachelor's thesis on SiGe antennas for vehicular radar. My technical-community work includes founding leadership in PUNTO and UC3-Base, payload and RF roles in ST3LLARSAT1/BOIRA, and former leadership in STAR UC3M.
thesisTitle: On-Chip SiGe Front Ends in Millimeter-Wave Bands for Automotive, Space and Communication Applications
